title: Choose the visual world for the Japan Plan C site
question: The roll assigned the Eki-Stamp Rally Card. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Eki-Stamp Rally Card
options.lineage: Japanese station stamp rallies (eki stamps, since 1931) and JR East's 2026 single-kanji crest stamps
options.thesis: The trip is a 16-stamp rally card: each day a kanji crest, stamped in vermilion as the group lives it.
materials: stamp-pad violet print on white card stock
options.viewport: Violet masthead with a live 'now / next' line, then the 16-circle stamp card (tap a day), then the route map.
options.risk: Stamps can turn cute if the timetable underneath is not set with real rigor.

raised.raise: Stamps are built from type alone: one kanji per place, name around the rim, no clip-art.
State is a mark, not a hue: solid ring booked, open ring still to book, dashed ring unconfirmed/TBA.
A 'you are here' flag marks the live stop; the site reopens where the group is right now.
One master grid for every day page; days differ only by their stamp.
Every day page repeats the same sections in a fixed order: opener, briefing, night-before check, timetable, map.

options.label: JR Timetable Book
options.lineage: the monthly JR/JTB 時刻表 timetable book with colored thumb-index tabs
options.thesis: The trip printed as a timetable book: dense time columns, red for the big nights, day tabs down the page edge.
options.viewport: Thumb tabs for the 16 days on the right edge, today's page open as a dense time table with the current row highlighted.
options.risk: Familiar: departure-board and timetable looks are where many travel sites land.

options.label: Cyclorama Days
options.lineage: theater cyclorama lighting cues, night to dawn to day
options.thesis: Each day is a lighting cue sheet: stops sit in horizon bands from pre-dawn departures to 3am karaoke.
options.viewport: A day as stacked horizon bands, the current band lit to day-white, sunset time drawn as the rose line.
options.case: Holds clarity: long 6am-to-4am days really do read better by light phase. Loses on identification: it isn't Japan or this group.
options.risk: Black-ground reading at night is great, but it reads theatrical rather than Japanese.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Day titles condense into weather over a white field.
options.risk: Performs over the timetable the group needs to read.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to Japan or the trip, and it fights reading.
options.kept: Type as the only image material: the stamps are pure lettering.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.thesis: Every stop tied to its default by an amber link line.
options.viewport: Numbered lanes under a fixed legend strip.
options.risk: A control-room costume on a travel guide.
options.case: Loses both: nobody in the group lives in a machine room.
options.kept: State drawn by stroke pattern, never by hue alone.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Days as frames on a perforated rail, a tape flag where you stopped.
options.viewport: A scrubbing frame strip across every screen.
options.risk: Scrubbing a film strip is slower than tapping a day.
options.case: Loses both: foreign to the audience, slower to find 'what's next'.

options.label: Swiss Poster Wall
options.thesis: Sixteen day-posters on one modular grid.
options.viewport: A wall of day posters, the current one in signal red.
options.risk: Cool and generic for a Japan trip.
options.case: Loses both: disciplined, but says nothing about Japan or these eight.
options.kept: One master grid governs every page.

options.label: Mid-century Magazine
options.thesis: Each day an issue with a hidden mark on its cover.
options.viewport: Serif masthead over a two-column grid.
options.risk: Magazine pacing slows the on-trip lookup.
options.case: Loses both: editorial nostalgia, slower lookups.
options.kept: Sections repeat in a fixed order on every day.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A trip-planner site done impeccably: photo hero, day-by-day cards, and a map.
canonCard.viewport: Big Japan photo hero with the trip title, then day cards and a map beside them.
canonCard.risk: Looks like Wanderlog or TripIt by design.
